audit.whatIsWrong: Full phases[5].side and phases[6].side read 'Skill' while content win[5] and win[6] read 'Zed'. The packet agrees with content.
audit.why: Zed is 51.44% over 4693 games and the edge arrives late: Death Mark plus a second shadow out-bursts Shadow Assault, and Talon's build stays squishy with no defensive layer beyond Assassin's Path.
audit.corrected: Both full sides moved to Zed. Their whys already described Zed winning those stages, and win[5]/win[6] already read Zed, so no paired content edits were proposed.

audit.whatIsWrong: First-item and two-item rows sat at 6/10 despite being the stages the page itself calls Zed's.
audit.why: Zed's spikes are level 6 and first-item lethality into a target with no resistances; Talon's are level 3 Blade's End stacking and his R roam window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions never reached the lane-facing fields. Assassin's Path has NO cooldown of its own — only the terrain it used goes on cooldown — so a marked Talon next to any wall simply vaults out and survives the three seconds. And Noxian Diplomacy refunds health AND cooldown when it kills, so every minion he executes with Q rearms his gap-closer mid-trade.
audit.why: Riot's E text: he vaults over any terrain, low cooldown, puts the used terrain on a long cooldown. Riot's Q text: refunds some health and cooldown if the ability kills the target.
audit.corrected: Written into tradeBad, breakdown.trading, dontsFull[2].d, breakdown.carry, ahead and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.why: The kit's derived flags mark Rake as 'knockup'. Riot's own text says the returning blades deal bonus damage and SLOW units hit — no displacement. Per the brief, the description wins.
audit.corrected: No knockup claim was written anywhere; the return pass is described as the damage and slow it actually is.
